# Best travel charger with multiple USB-C ports

**Top pick: UGREEN Nexode 100W (3× USB-C + 1× USB-A)**

Several reviewers name it the best overall for most travelers ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026), [Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/best-usb-c-phone-charger)).
- Either of the first two USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W alone.
- A laptop plus a second device splits to about 65W and 30W. With all four ports in use it's about 45W, 30W and 10.5W.
- It weighs 8.3 oz, which is the heaviest of the chargers compared. It has a foldable US plug and no cable in the box.
- One source (VoyageHacks) says it has four USB-C ports. Most sources, including TechWise and Android Central, list three USB-C plus one USB-A, so check the listing before buying.
- Where to buy: the "Check price" buttons on [TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) and [VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/). I wasn't given a direct product URL.

**Alternatives**

- **Anker Prime 67W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A):** The pick if you want something small. It weighs 4.78 oz, and either USB-C port can deliver the full 67W alone. It holds about 65W across two devices and 64.5W across three. It covers a MacBook Air-class laptop and a phone, but not a power-hungry laptop plus a tablet. [Details and buy link](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/)
- **Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A):** Better if one demanding laptop is your priority, since it has the most headroom. Power is still shared once more devices connect. [Details and buy link](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026)
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A), $49.99 for a 2-pack:** A budget option. Each USB-C port delivers 65W alone, but with two or three devices connected the laptop port drops to 45W, and the second USB-C port shares just 15W with the USB-A port. It's fine for a MacBook Air, less so for a 65W laptop. [Buy at Baseus (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u), [product details](https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u)

**If you travel abroad**

All of the chargers above have US-style foldable prongs, so you'll need a plug adapter. A plug adapter is enough, since these chargers accept 100-240V. If you'd rather have one device with swappable plugs, Android Central lists the Epicka TA-105 Max (75W, 3× USB-C + 2× USB-A) and the UGREEN 65W Nexode travel adapter (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A) ([guide](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel)).

**Tips**

- Put the laptop on a high-power USB-C port first, then add phones and earbuds.
- For 100W, use a 5A e-marked USB-C cable. Cheaper cables can limit the charger.
- If you have a Samsung or Pixel phone, choose a charger with PPS support.

Tell me which laptop and other devices you carry and I can narrow this to one pick.
